name: Gochujang Grilled Chicken Lettuce Wraps
why: Korean-inspired grilled chicken with a spicy-sweet gochujang marinade, served in crisp lettuce cups with quick-pickled carrots. Perfect summer dinner — light, bold, and hands-off once the chicken hits the grill.
author: Henry
ingredients: 2 lbs boneless skinless chicken thighs, trimmed
1-2 heads butter lettuce, leaves separated and dried
3 green onions, thinly sliced on the diagonal
2 mini cucumbers, thinly sliced on the diagonal

steps: In a large bowl, whisk together avocado oil, toasted sesame oil, coconut sugar, gochujang paste, coconut aminos, minced garlic, and grated ginger until well combined.
Transfer 1/3 cup of the marinade to a small bowl and set aside for serving.
Add chicken thighs and kosher salt to the remaining marinade. Toss until evenly coated.
Refrigerate for at least 30 minutes (or up to overnight for deeper flavor).
While chicken marinates, combine matchstick carrots, rice vinegar, and a pinch of salt in a small bowl.
Toss to coat and set aside — they'll quick-pickle while you cook.
Oil the grill grates: dip a wadded paper towel in oil and, using tongs, wipe evenly over the grate. Use sparingly to avoid flare-ups.
Place chicken on the grill, lid closed. Cook 4 minutes per side until golden with grill marks.
Flip once more, then reduce heat to medium-low (~300°F / 150°C) for 3-5 more minutes until internal temperature reaches 165°F (74°C).
Transfer chicken to a cutting board and rest for 5-8 minutes before slicing.
Lay out butter lettuce leaves on a platter alongside sliced green onions, cucumbers, cilantro, and pickled carrots.
Slice the rested chicken into strips or bite-sized pieces.
To serve: layer 2 lettuce leaves as a 'wrap', fill with pickled carrots and sliced chicken, top with cucumber slices, cilantro, and toasted sesame seeds.
Drizzle with reserved gochujang sauce and a squeeze of lime.

pro_tips: Marinate the chicken overnight for maximum flavor penetration — the gochujang and sesame oil work beautifully with extended time.
If you don't have coconut aminos, regular soy sauce works fine. For the sugar, brown sugar is a perfect substitute for coconut sugar.
